neighbours.label: predicts a staffed service point or storage place (reception, concierge, front desk, luggage room) in guest and visitor contexts
fire: After checking out, we left our suitcases with the porter until our train.
If you lose your key card, just ask at the front desk for a new one.
Guests can store their skis in the locked room next to the reception.
Our flight landed at midnight, but someone was still waiting at the desk to check us in.
You can drop off your coats at the cloakroom before the concert starts.
For theatre tickets and dinner bookings, speak to the concierge in the lobby.
Valuables should be left in the safe at reception during your stay.
When the elevator broke, we called down to the night manager for help.
quiet: After checking out, we walked along the river until our train.
If you get hungry, the town has several cheap noodle shops nearby.
Guests can swim in the heated pool next to the garden terrace.
Our flight landed at midnight, and the city lights looked beautiful from above.
The concert started late because the band was stuck in traffic.
For the best view of the old town, climb the hill behind the church.
The rooms were small but clean, with a view over the harbour.
When the rain stopped, we walked to the market for breakfast.

predictions: Guest/visitor sentences whose next word would be desk, reception, concierge or a place to leave belongings fire on the preceding token; sentences that set up no such place stay quiet.
notes: Logit effect promotes conc, reception, bell, storage, secure. Probe: 'on duty at the [front desk]' 1.098, 'leave your bags in the [hotel lobby]' 0.863, 'leave your bags in the [car]' 0.827 (setup alone fires), office 'loading dock' 0.456, 'concierge service' 0.555; library and volcano sentences 0.025. Near misses keep hotel/travel topics but remove the 'leave/ask at the ___' setup.
